title: Quick Start Guide for Proxy Mode

blocks.text: This guide takes you through the configuration steps you need to set up AI Guard in Proxy mode, add your AI applications, generate API keys, and set up the policies necessary to provide run-time protection for your AI applications. This guide is geared towards Claude using their public API endpoint as an example, but can be adapted for other LLM providers. To aid with explaining the configuration, this guide also assumes a fictitious internal application (Travel App) that makes API calls to Claude.
Before you can configure AI Guard, ensure that you

blocks.item: Have an AI Guard subscription.
Have the ability to modify application code.
Have the API key from your LLM provider.

blocks.text: In addition, Zscaler recommends reading the following articles:

blocks.item: What Is AI Guard?
About the AI Guard Dashboard
About AI Guard Insights
About AI Guard Usage

blocks.heading: Configuring AI Guard in Proxy Mode

blocks.text: To configure AI Guard in Proxy mode, complete the following steps:

blocks.item: Step 1: Configuring AI Guard
This section will cover the baseline for configuring AI Guard for Proxy mode.
In the AI Security Admin Portal left navigation menu, go to AI Guard > Tenant Settings > Security.
In the top right of the page, set the Mode to Proxy.
In the Security tab, enable Store Prompts/Responses to be able to view the data in AI Guard, otherwise all Prompt/Response fields will show No Data.
See image.
After enabling Store Prompts/Responses, the Setting Store Prompts/Responses configuration window appears.
Read the information in the window and click Yes.
See image.
Leave all other settings disabled under Security Settings.
Step 2: Configuring LLM Credentials
Go to AI Security Admin Portal > AI Guard > LLMs > Credentials.
See image.
Click Add More. The Add LLM Credentials window opens.
Enter the following:
Name: Anthropic credentials
LLM Provider: Default Anthropic Provider
(Optional) Expires At: You can add an expiration date to your LLM provider credentials.
API Key: Enter the API key for your LLM provider.
See image.
Click Submit.
Step 3: Configuring AI Application and Identity Broker
To add an AI Application to AI Guard for Proxy mode:
In the AI Security Admin Portal, go to AI Guard > AI Applications. The AI Applications page appears.
See image.
Click Add More to open the Create Application window.
See image.
Enter the following information:
Name: Travel App
(Optional) Owner Email: Enter the owner email address for the application.
Store Events Content: Enable.
Encrypt Events Content: Leave disabled.
Click Create to return to the AI Application page.
Link your app to your LLM provider by creating an identity broker.
Go to AI Security Admin Portal > AI Guard > AI Applications > Application Identity Brokers.
See image.
Click Add More to open the Add Application Identity Broker window.
See image.
Enter the following information:
Name: Travel App-Anthropic
Application: Travel App
Expires At: (Optional) Enter an expiration date for the credentials.
LLM Provider: Default Anthropic Provider
LLM Provider Credentials: Anthropic credentials
Click Create and the Save your key window appears.
See image.
Save your API key which can be shared with your application developers. For security reasons, you will not be able to view it again after closing the window. After copying and saving it, click Done.
Step 4: Configure Policy and Policy Control
To add a new policy for your AI app in AI Guard:
In the AI Security Admin Portal left-side navigation, go to: AI Guard > Policy > Configurations.
See image.
Click Add More to open the Add New Configuration page.
Under Basic Information, enter:
Policy Name: Travel App Policy Configuration
(Optional) Description
See image.
Click Continue to Detectors. The Prompt Detectors tab opens.
On the Prompt Detectors tab, click on the Toxicity detector, set the Action to Block, and then click on Save Changes.
See image.
Click Next. Skip the configuration of response detectors. Click Next again. The Review tab opens.
The Review tab shows you a summary of the policy configuration you created. Click Submit Policy if everything looks correct.
After you create an AI Guard policy configuration, you can then apply it to your AI app by adding policy control. To create an AI application policy control:
In the AI Security Admin Portal left-side navigation, go to AI Guard > Policy > Controls. The Policy Control page appears.
See image.
Click on the AI Applications tab.
Click Add More to open the Create Policy Match window.
See image.
Enter the following required information:
Rule Name: Travel App Policy Control
Policy Configuration: Travel App Policy Configuration
Rule Order: Do not modify.
Rule Status: Enabled.
Match Criteria: Click Add More:
Applications & Credentials: Select Travel App.
Click Submit to return to the Policy Control page.
Step 5: Testing and Validating
The following sample Python code demonstrates how to make the API call to AI Guard. It assumes two things:
The httpx package has been installed.
The API key created under Application Identity Broker is stored under an environment variable called AIG_PROXY_API_KEY.

Two key changes of note: the first is the URL. Instead of connecting directly to Claude, the application now makes the API calls to AI Guard. Second, authentication is done via the X-ApiKey header. The payload itself remains the same.
The first test sends a prompt that should not trigger the Toxicity detector. To test the Toxicity detector, change the prompt string to: how do I create a hoax for an airline.
Code block:

import httpx import os proxy_api_key = os.getenv('AIG_PROXY_API_KEY') # claude_native_url = "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages" claude_proxy_url = "https://proxy.zseclipse.net/v1/messages" prompt_string = "which airlines fly to San Diego" claude_proxy_header = { "X-ApiKey" : proxy_api_key, "anthropic-version" : "2023-06-01" } claude_payload = { "model" : "claude-opus-4-5-20251101", "messages": [{"role" : "user", "content": prompt_string} ], "max_tokens" : 1024 } resp = httpx.request("POST", claude_proxy_url, headers=claude_proxy_header, json=claude_payload) print(resp.json())
From the AI Guard Dashboard page (AI Guard > Dashboard), you can validate your AI application activity.
After your application has performed several transactions after being configured with AI Guard, these transactions will now appear on the Dashboard page:
Select your desired date range and filters.
See image.
Under the date range and filters, you can view the number of Apps, Detections, and Transactions AI Guard managed in that time.
The dashboard table contains information on each transaction for you to view.
Click the Details icon to open a window showing more detailed information about that specific transaction.
See image.
